reference.title: Dumbbell Standing Scapula External Rotation (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Back, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you rotate up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.progression: Add reps, then 0.5-1 kg; longer pause at the top

cues.text: Stand tall. Raise the right upper arm out to shoulder height, a little in front of the body, elbow bent 90 degrees, forearm pointing forward, palm down.
Breathe out and turn the forearm up like a hinge until it points to the ceiling; the elbow stays where it is.
Forearm vertical, palm forward, shoulder down away from the ear.
Lower slowly back to forearm level in about 2 s.
Pause with the forearm level and repeat; switch arms after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the elbow drop or drift
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arm level and still; only the forearm moves.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the back or leaning to finish
mistakes.fix: Use a lighter dumbbell and stop where the shoulder runs out of rotation.
Keep the shoulder blade down and back.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the wrist back to lift the weight
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist straight in line with the forearm.

kinematics.norm: About 90 degrees (Sung 2023 tested 45 and 90; 90 raised posterior deltoid and upper trapezius activity seated)
Scapular plane, a little in front of the frontal plane (clinical opinion)
From the forearm level (about 0 degrees) to the forearm vertical (about 90 degrees) (clinical opinion)
Slow, about 2 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #723412, Dumbbell Standing Scapula External Rotation (male), video (movement reference)
Sung, Jung, Wang and Kim 2023, the effects of body positions and abduction angles on shoulder muscle activity patterns during external rotation exercises (Healthcare 11(14):1977)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Sung 2023 tested sitting, supine and prone positions; standing values are inferred from the seated results.
Use very light weights: the rotator cuff is a small muscle group.
modify: Pain at 90 degrees: lower the elbow to about 45 degrees of abduction, which in Sung 2023 gave a better lower-to-upper trapezius balance.
Can not hold the arm up: rest the elbow on an incline bench pad (supported version) or do side-lying external rotation.
regressions: Elbow at the side with a band.
progressions: Slower lowering (3 s) and a 2 s pause at the top.

muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Prime mover (with teres minor): turns the upper arm out. Seated external rotation gave higher infraspinatus activity than supine at both 45 and 90 degrees of abduction (Sung 2023).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Prime mover (with teres minor): turns the upper arm out. Seated external rotation gave higher infraspinatus activity than supine at both 45 and 90 degrees of abduction (Sung 2023).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps rotate and holds the arm back in line; posterior deltoid activity seated was higher at 90 than at 45 degrees of abduction (Sung 2023).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps rotate and holds the arm back in line; posterior deltoid activity seated was higher at 90 than at 45 degrees of abduction (Sung 2023).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blade back so the upper arm stays in line with the body.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Hold the shoulder blade back so the upper arm stays in line with the body.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm up at shoulder height for the whole set.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arm up at shoulder height for the whole set.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Supports the shoulder blade; upper trapezius activity was higher at 90 than at 45 degrees of abduction (Sung 2023).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Supports the shoulder blade; upper trapezius activity was higher at 90 than at 45 degrees of abduction (Sung 2023).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blade on the ribs.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blade on the ribs.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still and the ribs down.

guides.label: Forearm turns up like a hinge
